prerequisites: Knowledge of differential calculus of single-variable functions
Knowledge of differential calculus of multi-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and classify bilinear forms and real quadratic forms.
Solve, using symbolic and numerical calculation, problems of maximums, minimums, and constrained extremes.
Decompose matrices, geometrically interpret the result, and apply it to problem-solving.
Utilize basic concepts, results, and techniques in affine and Euclidean geometry.
Relate the intuitive concept of rigid body motion (in the plane or in real space) with orthogonal transformations.
Explain the concept and know the usual techniques of least squares fitting.
Solve Advanced Mathematics problems using computational tools.

syllabus_topics: Orthogonality. Relation to rigid body motion.
Calculation of extremes of functions of several variables.
Numerical methods for the calculation of extremes.
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions (training videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
In-person expository classes (doubt resolution, theoretical development, examples)
Virtual classroom practices (video viewing, questionnaire answering, forum participation)
In-person classroom practices (individual or group exercises and tasks)
Virtual laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab software)
In-person laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab software)
Tutorials (forums, personal virtual tutoring via Teams)
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as NF = 0.2 NL + 0.2 NA + 0.5 NC + 0.1 NCv. NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, NC is the average of the partial exams (0.4 P1 + 0.6 P2) or the global exam grade (PG), and NCv is the virtual campus tasks grade. All grades are out of 10 points. The course is passed if NF >= 5, NC >= 3.5, and NL >= 3.5. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be min(NF, NC, NL). For differentiated evaluation, if classroom attendance is not possible, the formula becomes NF = 0.2 NL + 0.6 NC + 0.2 NOL, where NOL is the online tasks grade.
